# Issue #41: `slugify` produces double hyphens and trailing hyphens

`slugify("Hello,  World!")` returns `"hello--world-"` but should return `"hello-world"`.
Also `slugify("--a--b--")` should give `"a-b"`.

Please fix `textkit/slug.py`. Do not change the public signature.

The user wants to fix the `slugify` function in `textkit/slug.py`.
The current implementation has two issues:
1. It produces double hyphens when there are multiple non-alphanumeric characters.
2. It produces trailing hyphens when the input string ends with non-alphanumeric characters.

I need to modify the `slugify` function to address these issues.

Looking at the current regex `[^a-z0-9]`, it replaces any character that is not a lowercase letter or digit with a hyphen. This explains the double hyphens.
To fix this, I can first replace multiple hyphens with a single hyphen.
Then, to fix the trailing hyphens, I can strip hyphens from the beginning and end of the string.

Let's try to add these modifications.
I will add `re.sub(r"-+", "-", text)` to collapse multiple hyphens into one, and `text.strip("-")` to remove leading/trailing hyphens.
I will insert these lines after line 7.

```python
    text = text.lower()
    text = re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9]", "-", text)
    text = re.sub(r"-+", "-", text)  # Add this line
    text = text.strip("-")         # Add this line
    return text
```
